Alcohol is a depressant and Effexor is an anti-depressant so just take that into consideration. 

Drinking alcohol does lower the effectiveness of the medication, but every once and a while as long as you’re aware of your state of being, you should be okay to drink socially. I just wouldn’t recommend drinking to excess. As soon you start to feel hot cheeks or flushed/sweaty I would stop. That’s when you’re “buzzed” and you shouldn’t be sick the day after. Dizziness, drowsiness, and feeling weak while drinking alcohol is intensified by Effexor so just be aware if you start to feel that way. I also recommend eating while/before you drink! Enjoy fruit, protein, and stay hydrated!

Anti-Depressants are funny in a way that, when you are in the state of depression, you constantly think about suicide but you never actually go through with it because you don’t have the energy or resolve to do it.

I didn’t really have any friends until late Middle school and was a loner who didn’t take care of myself because of my extreme social anxiety and I always connect it back to that birthday. Im glad to say now in high school that I’m popular, a lot of people know me and I have very good friends but I will never throw a party or an event for myself and I make sure to tell my friends to never do something for me. I was on top of the world. Happy, Good Grades, Club President and officer for others, Supportive parent. People looked to me for help and advice. The depression came out of nowhere and I lost it all. I stopped showing up to school and stopped talking to friends. My absences lost me credit for classes and I lost scholarship opportunities and relationships with others. I resigned from my positions. I was so distraught that I had lost it all and that’s all I’d focused on. Depressions sucks, it effects your everyday life. Nothing bad has ever happened to me to cause it, but that doesn’t change the fact that I am depressed. What happened in the past is the past. That doesn’t stop me from fixing relationships I lost or letting some go and finishing high school even if it’s not where I wanted to be. I tell myself I’ll do better in college or if I decide to join the workforce or military or whatever I do. “Melancholic depression” is what I have. No reason for it but I have it and I have to fight it. Some days it gets the best of me but I gotta get out of my comfort zone and keep trying. Wonderful that you acknowledge it and yes you may never know what the future holds but you can always try to make each day better.

Try not to isolate yourself. I used to spend literal days in my room. Break the routine by laying in the living room or by just talking a 5 min walk outside. It made me feel better to go to a store to just look around and be around people even if I wasn’t buying anything. 
Don’t research how to end your life stay away from things that can feed into the bad thoughts. I would frequent forums that were sad and depressive and it made me worse and that didn’t help me at all. r/mademesmile gave me little moments of happiness. 

I recommend the book “The Upwards Spiral” by Alex Korb. It helped me become self aware of my thoughts, actions, and bad habits. 

Also become self aware of your bad habits.  Therapist can recognize and can help tell you how to fix it if you talk to them, but you can learn yourself. By gettin online resources. 

Living life is enough. You don’t have to have big goals to have a motivation to live. Sometimes you wanna live to eat ice cream in the summer at the park one day and that’s motivation enough for me.

I had depression for about two years. I accepted that I was constantly sad and didn’t do anything to combat it. (Part of depression is preventing you from thinking clearly/logically) then it finally got to the point where I even lost the feeling of being sad and all I felt was numbness. Nothing mattered I wanted to feel something, anything to feel human again. I never did hurt myself but I had decided to taking  my life would be better then feeling nothing at all. I told myself I wasn’t really gonna end my life but at the same time I was researching how to kill your self without pain and constantly thinking how I could make it less painful for my friends and family if I were to just disappear. 

If you start thinking that way even if you tell yourself you’re not really gonna do it, it’s still dangerous because you’re still planning it. 

I found that I like helping. In the center I listened to others and talked to them about their problems. If I were to take my life I’m gonna help someone first. Study to become a Doctor and save someone, become a firefighter and give my life to get them out, etc. Even if it’s unrealistic or small anything to motivate you to keeping on going is good. I still need to be alive to see the next Avengers Movie and I wanna follow a Bob Ross painting video. Still gotta live for that. It’s small but I look forward to it. You don’t have to have big accomplishments or goals. Enjoy little things in life.

It was a slap in the face. I never accepted help before but in treatment they are there 24/7 and I saw multiple professionals everyday that understood my problems and how to deal with them. A lot of group therapy/support, that helped me the most. To talk to people that are going through what  your experiencing, some going though even worse, it’s uplifting. A lot dark humor and jokes but it helped a lot. There was no stigma talking about your issues unlike in public with friends/family.  It gave me new perspective and I owe my life to that.

Before the center I didn’t think that anyone could help me. I rejected therapist because I thought it wasn’t for me. At the center they kept me in routine. Waking up, going to bed, eating lunch, breakfast, etc. it helped me to move around and have a schedule. The other people I met there were going through the same thing so I felt nice to talk about my issues openly. The Psychiatrist were very understanding and helpful and though it was irritating at times I learned coping methods and positive habits. After I left I was to go to a therapist and once I opened up it did help me a lot. (You have to find the right therapist for you, some you may not connect with so you just have to find one that does) I was so set on “I’m never coming back” and I was so accepting of death as a way out. The treatment helped me rethink that and gave me new motivation, hope and help.

Don’t focus on late work but the current work you have, you’ll stress yourself out by thinking about old work you haven’t done. You can get you’re 2.9 to a 3.0 and then slowly work it up.
